_notes: Second pass adds weapons, per Marky's stated priority order (weapons, flight controls, navigation, countermeasures). Same rule as the countermeasures pass: only add an entry once real bindings for it actually exist in data/bindings_live/ (checked 2026-09-06, both AH-64D pilot and CPG profile exports) - most weapon-specific controls (Weapons Trigger, WAS switch, Sight Select Switch, TADS/LRFD power, LRFD Trigger, Missile Type/Mode/Trajectory selectors) are NOT currently bound to any physical device in either seat's export, so those checklist/weapon steps correctly stay unannotated for now rather than guessed - Marky would need to bind those in DCS (or they're on keyboard only, which this app can't yet distinguish from unbound - see bindings.py). 'dcs_command' can be a single string or a list of equivalent strings, for cases where one binding_key legitimately matches more than one raw DCS command (different command IDs per seat, or the same page-select button existing separately on each MFD). Every string is copied exactly as it appears in the live export - including Chinese ones - since that's the real lookup key; 'display_label' (from data/dcs_command_translations.json where needed) is for display only.

cmws_arm_safe_arm.dcs_command: CMWS 红外干扰弹安全开关 - ARM

countermeasures_dispense_button.dcs_command: 红外干扰布撒按钮 - 按下
countermeasures_dispense_button.note: One physical DCS command covers both the checklist's 'Chaff Dispense Button' and 'Flare Dispense Button' references - on the real Apache (and in DCS) chaff and flares share one dispense button on the cyclic; the ASE page's armed mode decides which one actually comes out, not a separate physical control.

master_arm_as_pushbutton.note: Pilot seat's A/S command exports in Chinese ('A/S 按钮'), CPG seat's in English ('A/S Pushbutton') - both are bound to the same physical Button 81 on the throttle, so one binding_key covers both seats' version of this step.

fcr_fab.note: Two separate real commands (one per physical MFD) that do the same thing - press whichever MFD is showing the button. Both are bound (Left MFD and Center/Right MFD), so both show up as valid options.

collective_axis.note: An axis, not a discrete button - resolves to a physical device/axis (e.g. 'Axis RY, <throttle>'), not a press. Third pass, flight controls: checked for cyclic/pedal/trim/SAS/rotor-brake bindings too, but Collective was the only flight-control axis actually bound in the current export.
